description: The beastkin are animal-folk -- another of the continent's nonhuman kindreds, alongside the humans and the dragonkin. Where the dragonkin descend from a dragon-progenitor, the beastkin take the forms and natures of beasts. The HYENADIN (hyena-kin) are one such people, and a rival hostile to the dragonkin: it is their attack on the tribe's camp, near the story's end, that draws Kaelen into breaking his century of restraint and spends his life.
rules: Largely open -- built only as far as the story needs so far. Fixed: the hyenadin fall on the dragonkin camp on the mesa near the story's end, in Tomas's absence, and SLAUGHTER the fold. A defense-bound people cannot repel them (to fight back in earnest deepens the curse); Kaelen's aggressive fire kills many attackers but is not enough, and it kills him. Tomas, having left, returns too late to discover the aftermath, not to fight the battle.

details.The hyenadin: Hyena-beastkin. Rival and hostile to the dragonkin; the aggressors who slaughter the fold at the mesa. Dynamic: scavenger-predators who prey on the weak, drawn to a cursed, defense-bound people who cannot strike back without damning themselves -- the curse's defense-only law turned into a hunting weakness. They are seeded circling the mesa during the stay, and strike once Tomas (a fighter who could strike without curse-cost) has gone.
details.Open / to build later: Whether other beastkin peoples appear and what they are like; the beastkin's own nature, abilities, and culture; whether they are free or bound by any curse of their own; the specific reason the hyenadin hunt the dragonkin; how the climactic attack is set up earlier in the book so it does not arrive from nowhere.
